figures.title: Host Hardware and Driver Architecture
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the layered architecture of SD Host hardware and drivers, from applications at the top through card drivers, bus drivers, host controller driver, hardware registers, down to the SD card connector at the bottom.

figures.title: Classification of the Standard Register Map
figures.abstract: This figure shows the classification and memory layout of the SD Host Controller Standard Register Map, organized into 12 functional sections spanning address ranges from 0F-00h to FF-F0h with version-specific register groups.

figures.title: Register Map for Multiple Slots Controller
figures.abstract: This figure shows the register memory map organization for a multiple slot SD host controller, where each slot has its own standard register set (00-EF) and shares a common register area (F0-FF) accessible via independent base pointers.

figures.title: Suspend and Resume Mechanism
figures.abstract: This state diagram illustrates the SD card suspend and resume mechanism, showing how data transfer can be temporarily suspended to save register state, perform another data transfer operation, then restore the register state and resume the original transfer.

figures.title: Buffer Size Relation between Host and Card
figures.abstract: This block diagram illustrates the buffer relationship between the SD Host Controller and SD Card, connected via the SD Bus, showing that both entities maintain separate buffers for data transfer.

figures.title: Logical Relation for Interrupt Registers
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the logical relationship between interrupt control registers, where interrupt factors set a status register that enables interrupt signals and wakeup events, while interrupt clear resets the register.

figures.title: Block Diagram of Host Controller
figures.abstract: Block diagram showing the Host Controller architecture with System Bus Interface, Host IF (DMA), Buffer, Register Set, CMD Control, and DAT Control modules connected via a Buffer Interface to the SD Bus Interface.

figures.title: Block Diagram of ADMA2
figures.abstract: Block diagram showing ADMA2 architecture with System Address Register pointing to Descriptor Tables in system memory, which contain address/length/attribute entries linked to data blocks, with SDMA state machine generating DMA interrupts, ADMA errors, and transfer complete signals.

figures.title: An Example of ADMA2 Data Transfer
figures.abstract: This figure illustrates ADMA2 data transfer architecture showing how a descriptor table with address, length, and attribute fields maps to non-contiguous data blocks in system memory for SD multiple read/write operations.

figures.title: 32-bit Address Descriptor Table
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit address descriptor table structure with 64-bit entries containing address, length, reserved bits, action codes (Nop, Tran, Link), and attribute flags (Valid, End, Int) for ADMA operations.

figures.title: State Diagram of the ADMA2
figures.abstract: State diagram showing the four states of ADMA2 operation (Fetch Descriptor, Change Address, Transfer Data, and Stop ADMA) with transitions based on control flags and conditions.

figures.title: SDMA System Address / Argument 2 Register
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit SDMA System Address / Argument 2 Register layout (offset 000h) which stores either the physical memory address for SDMA transfers or the block count argument for Auto CMD23 operations.

figures.title: Block Size Register
figures.abstract: Block Size Register layout showing the reserved bit (D15), Host SDMA Buffer Boundary field (D14-12), and Transfer Block Size field (D11-00) with buffer boundary encoding values from 4K to 512K bytes.

figures.title: Block Count Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the 16-bit Block Count Register (offset 006h) used to configure the number of data blocks for SD Host Controller transfers.

figures.title: Argument 1 Register
figures.abstract: The Argument 1 Register (offset 008h) is a 32-bit read/write register containing the SD command argument specified as bits 39-8 of the Command-Format in the Physical Layer Specification.

figures.title: Transfer Mode Register
figures.abstract: The Transfer Mode Register (offset 00Ch) is a 16-bit register that controls data transfer operations including block selection, transfer direction, auto command enable, block count enable, and DMA enable settings.

figures.title: Command Register
figures.abstract: The Command Register (offset 00Eh) is a 16-bit register that specifies the SD command parameters including command index, command type (Normal/Suspend/Resume/Abort), data presence, and response type selection.

figures.title: Response Register
figures.abstract: The Response Register is a 128-bit register organized across four 32-bit offsets (010h-01Ch) that stores command responses from SD cards, with bits numbered from D00 to D31 in each offset.

figures.title: Buffer Data Port Register
figures.abstract: A 32-bit register layout showing the Buffer Data Port Register (offset 020h) with bits D31 to D00 used for accessing the Host Controller's internal buffer.

figures.title: Present State Register
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit Present State Register layout at offset 024h, displaying status bits for CMD/DAT line signals, card detection, buffer states, and transfer activity indicators.

figures.title: Card Detect State
figures.abstract: This state diagram shows the card detection debouncing logic in an SD Host Controller, transitioning from Reset through Debouncing to either Card Inserted or No Card states based on the stable SDCD# signal.

figures.title: Timing of Command Inhibit (DAT) and Command Inhibit (CMD) with Data Transfer
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the relationship between CMD line command/response phases and DAT line data transfer phases, with D00 and D01 signal transitions during write or read data operations ending with last block data.

figures.title: Timing of Command Inhibit (DAT) for the Case of Response with Busy
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the Command Inhibit (DAT) behavior when a response includes a busy signal, with DAT[0] going busy after the response while data lines D00 and D01 transition accordingly.

figures.title: Timing of Command Inhibit (CMD) for the Case of No Response Command
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the Command Inhibit (CMD) signal behavior where the host controller clears the D00 line after successfully issuing a command that expects no response.

figures.title: Host Control 1 Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the 8-bit Host Control 1 Register at offset 028h with bit field assignments for card detection, data transfer width, DMA selection, high speed enable, and LED control.

figures.title: Power Control Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the Power Control Register at offset 029h with bit fields for SD Bus Voltage Select (D03-D01) and SD Bus Power control (D00).

figures.title: Block Gap Control Register
figures.abstract: Block Gap Control Register layout showing bit fields for interrupt control, read wait control, continue request, and stop at block gap request functionality in an SD Host Controller.

figures.title: Wakeup Control Register
figures.abstract: The Wakeup Control Register (offset 02Bh) is an 8-bit register that enables wakeup events for SD card removal, insertion, and card interrupt through three control bits (bits 0-2), with the upper bits reserved.

figures.title: Clock Control Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 16-bit Clock Control Register at offset 02Ch, which controls SDCLK frequency selection, clock generator mode, and internal/SD clock enable status for the SD Host Controller.

figures.title: Timeout Control Register
figures.abstract: Register layout showing the Timeout Control Register at offset 02Eh with a 4-bit reserved field (D07-D04) and a 4-bit Data Timeout Counter Value field (D03-D00) that configures DAT line timeout intervals using TMCLK-based exponential values.

figures.title: Software Reset Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the Software Reset Register (offset 02Fh) with bit fields for resetting the DAT line, CMD line, and all controller components.

figures.title: Normal Interrupt Status Register
figures.abstract: The Normal Interrupt Status Register (offset 030h) is a 16-bit register layout showing interrupt status bits for SD host controller operations including error, re-tuning, card detection, buffer ready, DMA, transfer and command completion events.

figures.title: Error Interrupt Status Register
figures.abstract: The Error Interrupt Status Register (offset 032h) is a 16-bit register layout showing various error status bits including vendor-specific errors, tuning error, ADMA error, and command/data transfer errors with their respective bit positions and access attributes.

figures.title: Normal Interrupt Status Enable Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 16-bit Normal Interrupt Status Enable Register at offset 034h, which controls enabling/masking of various SD host controller interrupt sources including card events, buffer ready signals, DMA interrupts, and transfer completion status.

figures.title: Error Interrupt Status Enable Register
figures.abstract: Register layout showing the 16-bit Error Interrupt Status Enable Register with individual bit fields for enabling/masking various SD host controller error interrupt types.

figures.title: Normal Interrupt Signal Enable Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 16-bit Normal Interrupt Signal Enable Register at offset 038h, where each bit (except bit 15 fixed to 0 and bits 14-13 reserved) controls enabling/masking of specific interrupt signals to the host system.

figures.title: Error Interrupt Signal Enable Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 16-bit Error Interrupt Signal Enable Register at offset 03Ah, which controls which error status conditions generate interrupts to the host system, with individual enable bits for various error types including command, data, ADMA, and tuning errors.

figures.title: Auto CMD Error Status Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the Auto CMD Error Status Register (offset 03Ch) which indicates CMD12 and CMD23 response errors for Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 operations with individual error status bits for timeout, CRC, end bit, index, and command not issued errors.

figures.title: Host Control 2 Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the 16-bit Host Control 2 Register at offset 03Eh with bit field assignments including Preset Value Enable, Asynchronous Interrupt Enable, Driver Strength Select, Execute Tuning, and UHS Mode Select fields.

figures.title: Sampling Clock Tuning Procedure
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sampling clock tuning procedure for SD host controllers, including the sequence of issuing CMD19, checking buffer ready status, and determining tuning completion or failure based on Execute Tuning and Sampling Clock Select flags.

figures.title: Capabilities Register
figures.abstract: The Capabilities Register (offset 040h) is a 64-bit register layout showing host controller implementation features including clock configuration, voltage support, DMA capabilities, speed modes, driver types, and re-tuning modes.

figures.title: Maximum Current Capabilities Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 64-bit Maximum Current Capabilities Register at offset 048h, with three 8-bit fields specifying maximum current support for 1.8V, 3.0V, and 3.3V voltage levels, and reserved bits in the upper portion.

figures.title: Force Event Register for Auto CMD Error Status
figures.abstract: Register layout showing the 16-bit Force Event Register for Auto CMD Error Status with write-only bit fields that generate interrupts for various Auto CMD error conditions when set to 1.

figures.title: Force Event Register for Error Interrupt Status
figures.abstract: Register layout showing the 16-bit Force Event Register for Error Interrupt Status with write-only bit fields for forcing various error interrupt conditions in an SD Host Controller.

figures.title: ADMA Error Status Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the ADMA Error Status Register at offset 054h with fields for reserved bits, ADMA Length Mismatch Error, and ADMA Error States.

figures.title: ADMA System Address Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 64-bit ADMA System Address Register at offset 058h, which holds the physical descriptor address for ADMA data transfers with separate mappings for 32-bit and 64-bit addressing modes.

figures.title: Fields of A Preset Value Register
figures.abstract: Figure 2-36 shows the bit field layout of a Preset Value Register with fields for Driver Strength Select (D15-D14), Reserved bits (D13, D11), Clock Generator Select (D10), and SDCLK Frequency Select Value (D09-D00).

figures.title: Shared Bus Control Register
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the 32-bit Shared Bus Control Register at offset 0E0h with fields for back-end power control, clock pin select, bus width preset, and interrupt input pin configuration.

figures.title: An Example Timing of Selecting Clock Pin
figures.abstract: This timing diagram illustrates how the Clock Pin Select register controls which SDCLK pins (CLK[1], CLK[2], CLK[3]) generate clock signals for device selection in a shared bus system.

figures.title: Slot Interrupt Status Register
figures.abstract: The Slot Interrupt Status Register is a 16-bit register where bits 07-00 indicate interrupt signals for up to 8 slots (one bit per slot), with bits 15-08 reserved.

figures.title: Host Controller Version Register
figures.abstract: This register layout shows the 16-bit Host Controller Version Register at offset 0FEh, with the upper byte reserved for vendor version and the lower byte encoding the SD Host Controller specification version (1.00, 2.00, or 3.00).

figures.title: Double Box Notation
figures.abstract: The double box notation indicates that other flows (already shown elsewhere) shall be performed at that step, allowing interrupts to be included within those referenced flows.

figures.title: SD Card Detect Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD card detection sequence, which enables card detection interrupts, waits for the interrupt, clears the status, and checks whether a card insertion or removal occurred.

figures.title: SD Clock Supply Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Clock Supply Sequence for initializing and enabling the SD clock to an SD card, including calculating the divisor, setting frequency select, waiting for clock stability, and enabling clock output.

figures.title: SD Clock Stop Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Clock Stop Sequence, which involves setting the SD Clock Enable bit to 0 in the Clock Control register to stop supplying the SD Clock.

figures.title: SD Clock Change Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the two-step sequence for changing the SD Clock frequency: first stopping the SD clock, then supplying the new SD clock.

figures.title: SD Bus Power Control Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Bus Power Control Sequence for initializing and managing voltage settings between the host controller and SD card, including voltage negotiation and power control steps.

figures.title: Change Bus Width Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence of steps required to change the bus width on an SD card interface, including disabling interrupts, changing bit modes for both card and host, and re-enabling interrupts with different paths for SD memory-only cards versus other card types.

figures.title: Timeout Setting Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the two-step sequence for configuring timeout detection on the DAT line before SD transactions, involving calculating a timeout divisor from the Capabilities register and setting the Data Timeout Counter Value in the Timeout Control register.

figures.title: Card Initialization and Identification
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD card initialization and identification procedure, including voltage window negotiation, card type detection (SDSC/SDHC/SDXC/SDIO), and the sequence of commands (ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3) used to identify and configure the card.

figures.title: Signal Voltage Switch Procedure
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Host Controller signal voltage switch procedure from 3.3V to 1.8V signaling, including command execution, clock control, voltage enable, and verification steps.

figures.title: SD Command Issue Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence for issuing an SD command, including checking CMD/DAT line availability, handling abort conditions, and setting argument and command registers before completing the command sequence.

figures.title: Command Complete Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence to finalize an SD command, including waiting for command complete interrupt, checking for transfer complete interrupt if needed, and validating response data before returning status.

figures.title: Transaction Control with Data Transfer Using DAT Line Sequence (Not using DMA)
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Host Controller transaction control sequence for data transfer using the DAT line without DMA, including register setup, command execution, buffer ready interrupts for read/write operations, and transfer completion handling.

figures.title: Transaction Control with Data Transfer Using DAT Line Sequence (Using SDMA)
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence of register configuration steps and interrupt handling required to perform an SDMA (System DMA) data transfer transaction on an SD host controller.

figures.title: Transaction Control with Data Transfer Using DAT Line Sequence (Using ADMA)
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence of operations for performing data transfer using ADMA (Advanced DMA) in an SD Host Controller, including descriptor setup, register configuration, command execution, and interrupt handling for both successful completion and error conditions.

figures.title: Asynchronous Abort Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the asynchronous abort sequence for SD host controllers, which issues an abort command and then performs software reset on DAT and CMD lines until both reset flags are cleared.

figures.title: Synchronous Abort Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the synchronous abort sequence for SD host controller operations, including setting block gap request, waiting for transfer completion, issuing abort command, and performing software reset for DAT and CMD lines.

figures.title: High Speed Mode Setting for Combo Card
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the sequence for switching bus speed modes (Default, High Speed, UHS-I) for Combo Cards using CMD6 for memory and EHS/BSS[2:0] bits in CCCR for SDIO.

figures.title: Error Report and Recovery
figures.abstract: This block diagram illustrates the error reporting and recovery mechanism between the SD Host Controller and SDIO Card, showing how error and normal interrupt status registers trigger recovery processes in both the host and card drivers.

figures.title: Return Status of Auto CMD12 Error Recovery
figures.abstract: This state diagram shows four different error recovery scenarios (Return A-D) for Auto CMD12 command execution, illustrating the flow between CMD_wo_DAT, Auto CMD12, and CMD12 states with their respective error conditions and interrupt timing points.

figures.title: Error Interrupt Recovery Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the error interrupt recovery sequence for an SD host controller, detailing the steps from issuing an abort command through checking various error conditions to returning either recoverable or non-recoverable error status.

figures.title: Auto CMD12 Error Recovery Sequence
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the Auto CMD12 error recovery sequence for SD host controllers, detailing the decision paths and actions taken based on command execution status, error types, and software reset operations.

figures.title: Wakeup Control before Standby Mode
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the three-step sequence for preparing wakeup control before the SD Host System enters standby mode, including setting 1-bit mode, stopping the SD clock, and enabling wakeup factors.

figures.title: Wakeup from Standby
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the four-step sequence for waking up an SD host controller from standby mode, including waiting for wakeup event, disabling factors, supplying SD clock, and changing bus width.

figures.title: The Sequence for Suspend
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the suspend sequence for an SD Host Controller, including block gap request handling, interrupt waiting, bus status checking, and register saving operations.

figures.title: The Sequence for Resume
figures.abstract: This flowchart shows the SD Host Controller resume sequence, which restores registers, issues a resume command, checks the data flag, and conditionally performs a software reset for the DAT line.

figures.title: Wait Read Transfer by Stop At Block Gap Request
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the signal sequence for pausing a read transfer at a block gap using the Stop At Block Gap Request control signal, including the generation of Block Gap Event and Transfer Complete interrupts.

figures.title: Stop At Block Gap Request is Not Accepted at the Last Block of the Read Transfer
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows that when Stop At Block Gap Request is asserted during the last block transfer, the Host Controller ignores the request, completes the transfer normally without generating a Block Gap Event interrupt, and generates only the Transfer Complete interrupt.

figures.title: Continue Read Transfer by Continue Request
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows how a stopped read transfer is restarted by asserting the Continue Request control signal, which releases Read Wait and reactivates the DAT line and Read Transfer Active status until Transfer Complete.

figures.title: Wait Write Transfer by Stop At Block Gap Request
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the signal sequence for a write transaction wait/continue operation when a Stop At Block Gap Request is issued, illustrating the coordination between control signals, status signals, and interrupts during the block gap handling process.

figures.title: Stop At Block Gap Request is Not Accepted at the Last Block of the Write Transfer
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows that when Stop At Block Gap Request is asserted during the last block of a write transfer, the host controller ignores the request, completes the transfer normally without generating a Block Gap Event interrupt, and only generates the Transfer Complete interrupt.

figures.title: Continue Write Transfer by Continue Request
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows how a stopped write transfer is restarted using the Continue Request control signal, which re-activates the DAT Line Active and Write Transfer Active status signals to resume data transmission.
